interest: Documents U.S. Open Door enforcement resisting American oil sales, alongside consular intelligence on Manchuria's refinery defects and Japanese regulations.
overview: This file documents the establishment and administrative implementation of the petroleum monopoly in Manchuria and its extension into the Kwantung Leased Territory and the South Manchuria Railway Zone between October 1934 and May 1935. It details the construction, technical defects, initial operations, and supply contracts of the Manchuria Oil Company's refinery at Kanseishi near Dairen, as well as Japanese regulatory frameworks such as Kwantung Bureau Ordinance No. 23 governing petroleum import, testing, and storage. Throughout the correspondence, the U.S. State Department consistently enforced policy refusing diplomatic facilitation to American petroleum companies attempting to supply the monopoly, citing violations of American treaty rights and the Open Door policy.
